metadata.description: A CPU: a physical socket, or a virtual CPU presented to a guest. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): Redfish Processor (ProcessorType CPU) abstracts over both, so cores of a given architecture are one deliverable any host or hypervisor provider presents. An inventory component: the host carries the cpu rollup and may also contain Processor records; outputs-exempt: it publishes no realize-time binding surface (rule 36(b) documented exclusion).

device_class.description: Device realization (common-elements.md §7): `physical` (a socket), `virtual` (a vCPU), or `partition` (a pinned set carved from a parent).

partition_mechanism.description: How a partition is carved, when `device_class` is partition: `cpu-pinning` or `cpu-set`.

location.description: Socket designation within the parent, e.g. CPU1 (Redfish Socket). Primary discriminator.

model.description: Processor model, e.g. AMD EPYC 7443P (Redfish Model).

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The host this processor is installed in; parent carries the reconciled cpu rollup (§26).

relationships.name: guest
relationships.description: For device_class=virtual, the guest the vCPU is presented to.

adopts.role: processor component vocabulary (cores, threads, architecture, speed, socket)

context.purpose: Inventories a CPU — a physical socket or a vCPU presented to a guest — as a first-class component when the host rollup is not enough.
context.plain_description: One processor as its own record: `cores` (required), `threads`, `architecture`, and its clock as `max_speed_mhz`. Identity facts — model, location (the socket designation), serial — nest under the `identity` block, not at the top level. Most estates only need the aggregate CPU numbers already carried on the host; this type exists for when a socket must be individually addressable (asset tracking, heterogeneous sockets). device_class distinguishes the physical socket from a virtual CPU presented to a guest. Nothing binds to a processor at runtime, so it publishes no outputs — it is inventory.
use_when: You need per-socket inventory (exact model, position, serial) beyond the host's aggregate core/thread rollup.
You need virtual CPUs presented to a guest tracked as components.
not_for: Ordinary capacity accounting — the cpu rollup on Machine.BareMetalHost covers that without per-socket records.
works_with: Machine.BareMetalHost — the host the socket is installed in, which carries the reconciled rollup.
Machine.VM — the guest a virtual CPU is presented to.
